source: Sources: ANS Nuclear Newswire, Daily Galaxy (24 Nov 2026)

scenes.vo: NASA wants a nuclear reactor on the Moon. Here's why solar isn't enough.
scenes.cap: NASA wants a nuclear reactor on the Moon. Why not solar?

scenes.vo: It's called Lunar Reactor One. Target power: twenty kilowatts, electric.
The problem is night. At the lunar south pole, it must survive at least fourteen point seven five days of continuous darkness. Solar panels get nothing.
scenes.cap: Must survive at least 14.75 days of continuous darkness

scenes.vo: Batteries for two weeks of night get huge and heavy. A reactor runs the same, day or night.
scenes.cap: 2 weeks of batteries = heavy. A reactor runs day or night.

scenes.vo: Twenty kilowatts is roughly what sixteen average American homes use. Enough for a small base.
scenes.cap: 20 kW is roughly 16 average American homes

scenes.vo: Rules: run five years with no maintenance, keep working after a single failure, and keep crew radiation low a kilometre away.
scenes.cap: 5 years, no maintenance. Works after a single failure.

scenes.vo: Target: launch ready by December twenty thirty. Proposals are due this December twenty first. Would you live next to it?
scenes.cap: Launch-ready target: Dec 2030. Proposals due 21 Dec 2026.
